name: Pi-hole HA Cluster
tagline: Pi-hole DHCP high-availability cluster with automatic failover
description: Pi-hole HA Cluster turns a single Pi-hole into a high-availability DHCP cluster with automatic failover, a virtual IP, and configuration synchronization. A web UI and CLI let you add and remove nodes, set a manual master override, and watch each node's role — PRIMARY or STANDBY. When the active node dies or is removed, the cluster elects a new primary, claims the shared virtual IP, and takes over DHCP duty so clients keep getting addresses. The system also syncs Pi-hole configuration across nodes and periodically pulls down-to-date IEEE and OUI vendor databases for device identification. A node with no peers deliberately never runs failover logic, and a removed node steps down rather than competing, so the cluster cannot split and start a second DHCP server on the network.
highlights: Automatic failover with shared virtual IP and config sync across nodes
Web UI and CLI for cluster membership, master override, and role monitoring
DHCP continuity — a STANDBY node takes over if the PRIMARY stops serving
Periodic IEEE and OUI vendor database updates for device identification
Split-brain-safe: standalone and removed nodes never seize the VIP or run a second DHCP server
curatorNote: This fills a real home-lab gap: Pi-hole is famously single-node, and this project adds high-availability failover, a virtual IP, and config sync with just 66 stars. It is precisely the kind of niche infrastructure tool this catalog exists to surface.
